title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Improving Accountability and Member Outcomes in Superannuation Measures No. 2) Bill 2017
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Improving Accountability and Member Outcomes in Superannuation Measures No. 2) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend choice of superannuation fund to more employees and prevent salary sacrifice arrangements from reducing employers' compulsory contribution obligations for their workers.
Employers would calculate compulsory contributions using earnings before amounts sacrificed into superannuation, and could not count those sacrificed contributions towards their own minimum payments.
Fund choice changes would cover workplace determinations and enterprise agreements made from 1 July 2018, while existing exemptions for specified defined benefit members would remain.
changes: New employees covered by the expanded choice rules would receive a standard choice form.
Existing employees could request a choice form when a new covered agreement or determination is made.
Terms restricting choice in covered new agreements could not prevent contributions to the employee's chosen fund.
Salary sacrificed contributions paid late could not offset an employer's superannuation guarantee charge.
summary.affected: Employees under covered industrial instruments, people salary sacrificing into superannuation, employers and superannuation funds would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Improving Accountability and Member Outcomes in Superannuation Measures No. 2) Bill 2017 was not opposed by Labor in the House, with support for closing the salary sacrifice loophole and a reserved position on choice of fund until the Senate Economics Legislation Committee reports. The speaker noted that unpaid superannuation affects 2.4 million workers, costing them $5.6 billion annually.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Improving Accountability and Member Outcomes in Superannuation Measures No. 2) Bill 2017, which includes two measures from their own private member's bill: closing a loophole that allowed employers to count salary sacrifice contributions as employer contributions, and giving employees the choice of super fund in workplace determinations and enterprise agreements. The speaker argued the bill does not go far enough, called for employees to have a direct right of action to recover unpaid superannuation rather than relying on the Australian Taxation Office, and urged the government to adopt further provisions from their private member's bill.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill's two main provisions: giving employees the right to choose their superannuation fund, ending forced default funds under enterprise agreements, and closing loopholes that allow employers to reduce super guarantee contributions based on salary sacrifice amounts. They also argued for requiring superannuation fund boards to have at least one-third independent directors, including an independent chair, to improve governance.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Improving Accountability and Member Outcomes in Superannuation Measures No. 2) Bill 2017 extends choice of superannuation fund to over one million Australians covered by federal enterprise bargaining agreements and closes a loophole preventing employers from using salary sacrifice contributions to reduce their superannuation guarantee obligations.
